bib.title: PROMETHEUS 2: An Open Source Language Model Specialized in Evaluating Other Language Models

read.skipped: Reference list (chars ~38400-49900) skimmed for lineage only.

question: Can an open-source LM be trained as a unified evaluator that matches human and GPT-4 judgements in both direct assessment and pairwise ranking with custom criteria?
hypothesis: Merging the weights of evaluator LMs trained separately on direct assessment and pairwise ranking yields a unified evaluator that beats joint training and single-format training.
contributions: Prometheus 2 (7B & 8x7B), open evaluator LMs with high correlation with humans and proprietary judges in both formats.
The Preference Collection, a pairwise ranking feedback dataset with 1K custom evaluation criteria.
Showing that weight merging of direct-assessment and pairwise-ranking evaluators gives a unified evaluator that excels in both.

method.summary: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 and Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1 are fine-tuned separately on the Feedback Collection (direct assessment) and the new Preference Collection (pairwise), then merged (linear alpha=0.5 for 7B, DARE for 8x7B). Evaluated on four direct-assessment and four pairwise benchmarks against open and proprietary evaluators.

prompts.text: ###Task Description: An instruction (might include an Input inside it), a response to evaluate, and a score rubric representing a evaluation criteria are given. 1. Write a detailed feedback that assess the quality of the response strictly based on the given score rubric, not evaluating in general. 2. After writing a feedback, write a score that is an integer between 1 and 5. You should refer to the score rubric. 3. The output format should look as follows: "Feedback: (write a feedback for criteria) [RESULT] (an integer number between 1 and 5)" 4. Please do not generate any other opening, closing, and explanations. ###The instruction to evaluate: {orig_instruction} ###Response to evaluate: {orig_response} ###Score Rubrics: {score_rubric} ###Feedback:

Training used about 800 GPU hours on eight 40GB A100s.

limits: Evaluator quality is measured indirectly, by agreement with humans or GPT-4/Claude-3-Opus, which may not be the best approach.
Generalisation rests on overlap analysis from Kim et al. (2023); human-judgment benchmarks are scarce.
Only 1-5 Likert and A/B formats; no 1-10 scale, five-way ranking or checklist evaluation.
Why weight merging works is not explained; Section 6 is indirect.
DARE-Linear chosen from 7B ablation and applied to 8x7B without further tests due to compute.
Preference Collection is English only and its feedback is GPT-4-1106 generated (OpenAI terms).
Results on the 8x7B still trail GPT-4-1106 and Claude-3-Opus on pairwise benchmarks (e.g. HHH 85.52 vs 90.95).
Authors say model-based evaluation should be used alongside human evaluation.
